channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: New library books: Danielle Steel's 'The Color of Hope' added to collection
item.description: The Wilson County Public Library adds new adult fiction, nonfiction, young adult, Spanish, and children’s titles, from Danielle Steel and Lee Child to Dav Pilkey and Jenny Colgan.

item.title: 2 artists share gallery space in Barton exhibit
item.description: Barton Art Galleries presents “Parallel Origins,” a dual-artist exhibit and residency featuring Robert Smith and José Bayro C., whose distinct works explore memory, material and personal history, opening Thursday with a free public reception.

item.title: Schools prepare students for new biotech jobs here
item.description: Wilson Community College and five high schools are training students through a BioWork course for biotech and pharmaceutical jobs, including roles at Johnson & Johnson’s new Wilson County manufacturing facilities.

item.title: Officials call laundromat fire intentional
item.description: Fire officials say an intentional blaze at The Wash House laundromat on Downing Street caused $16,000 in damage early Monday but was quickly contained, and the business reopened.

item.title: Our Opinion: Wilson council members should place service above enforcement
item.description: A Wilson Times editorial faults Councilman Lenwood Ward and Mayor Carlton Stevens for overstepping their authority as elected officials, urging council members to focus on advocacy and policymaking.

item.title: When life hands Trump the Epstein files, Trump makes Lemon aid
item.description: As journalists are arrested at a Minnesota church protest and Trump declares a Cuba “emergency,” the DOJ releases millions of Epstein files, thousands naming Trump and prompting questions about what remains unreleased.

item.title: Keep recent economic news in perspective
item.description: North Carolina’s GDP surge, population gains and new factory projects make headlines, but decade-long trends in growth, migration and manufacturing paint a more cautious economic picture.

item.title: Good riddance to a bad actor at UNC
item.description: A Carolina Forward policy analyst argues that departing trustee John Preyer damaged UNC-Chapel Hill through partisan activism, from pushing a conservative civics school to undermining faculty tenure.

item.title: Hospitals set the prices, the legislature sets the rules
item.description: Hospital prices have jumped 256% since 2000, far outpacing inflation. An N.C. Republican leader argues that a broken market requires tougher legislative rules on transparency, consolidation and hospital costs.
